request.system: You are a sceptical results reviewer. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Pick the configuration to carry forward. Prefer a simpler model unless a more complex one is better by more than one standard deviation of PR-AUC across folds. Flag any result that looks too good. You may request up to 0 more round(s) of experiments; set stop=true if further search is unlikely to help. Rate your confidence in chosen_run (0-1): 1.0 means results are clear-cut and no reasonable reviewer would disagree; 0.5 means the top configs are too close to call or something looks off. You can inspect the per-fold PR-AUC breakdown of any completed run to assess consistency. A config that wins consistently across folds is more trustworthy than one with high variance. (Independent run 1.)

concerns: Run 2 (LightGBM, all+agent) beats run 1 (random forest, all) by 0.028 PR-AUC. That is under one fold SD (0.056 to 0.065), so the simplicity rule favours the random forest with fewer features and no boosting tuning.

Run 2 beats run 1 on all 5 folds (paired gaps of about 0.012 to 0.044). The paired evidence is therefore more consistent than the unpaired SD suggests, and a reasonable reviewer could pick run 2. Confidence is moderate for this reason.
Run 3 is the weakest (0.7009) and has the highest variance (SD 0.079), so it is not a contender.

ROC-AUC of about 0.94 and PR-AUC of about 0.70-0.73 at a 9.35% base rate are strong for an undocumented label. The label may be derived from provider-level rules or volume statistics, so the models may be reproducing the labelling process rather than detecting fraud. Size features and the agent features are possible leakage or proxy channels.
The PotentialFraud label is a suspicion flag, not confirmed fraud. The reported metrics measure agreement with that flag, not audit yield.
Only 3 configs were tried, with no logistic baseline and no no_size run without agent features. The simplicity comparison is therefore incomplete.
Folds are large-variance (PR-AUC from 0.60 to 0.79), and the claims window is under 13 months. If folds are not time-aware or grouped, optimistic estimates are possible.
Precision@50 was reported but the queue holds about 100, so top-100 precision is not directly verified. The prec@50 gap (0.748 vs 0.776) is small.
No further rounds are available, so stop is set to true.
